summary: Map v4 is accepted with the corrected transport boundaries, all four obligations remain disposed (three confirmed in-scope violations and one reviewed bounded no-violation), and there is no pending work or open issue. New obligation capacity is exhausted, so this step continues the authorized source work on the surface that was just reclassified as deferred. Submission is a feedback-only research product (no map version) that partially bounds the library's own transport. Reading: NetworkTransport.Consumer returns the internal channel the main loop reads; LocalAddr derives from the stream address and IsShutdown probes shutdownCh (net_transport.go 346-364); AppendEntries, RequestVote, RequestPreVote and TimeoutNow all delegate to genericRPC (468-484), which takes a connection through getConnFromAddressProvider, applies n.timeout as a connection deadline, sends the typed RPC and decodes the typed response, while InstallSnapshot has its own streaming path (509-546); AppendEntriesPipeline returns ErrPipelineReplicationNotSupported when maxInFlight is below minInFlightForPipelining and otherwise builds a netPipeline over one connection with maxInFlight outstanding requests (450-465, newNetPipeline at 814-817); SetHeartbeatHandler stores the fast-path callback under a mutex (298-306). The feedback ties this to the deferred surface by id and states plainly that nothing was evaluated for defects and no requirement or confirmed result changes. The remaining list names what is still unread and therefore keeps the surface deferred: netPipeline internals (in-flight bounding, response correlation, consumer ordering), the connection pool lifecycle (getConn/getPooledConn/returnConn, reconnect and dead-connection handling, mid-stream failures), the listen/dispatch path (RPC type dispatch and per-message-type queueing into consumeCh, including back-pressure), TCPTransport's TLS and configuration wiring, and InmemTransport's in-process delivery and ordering semantics, with the note that inmem_transport.go is the transport the captured tests exercise and therefore underpins the harness evidence rather than being library-external. Preflight validation returns valid with no diagnostics.
